observations: All eight current renders are explicitly diagnostic partial displays labeled “Missing display parts: chair_body.”
Views 1–6 show only four brown, straight, square legs with exposed upper mounting tabs. Views 7 and 8 likewise show only the four-leg footprint from above and below.

The legs appear symmetrically arranged and broadly consistent in length and section, but the absent mating body prevents meaningful visual assessment of the complete assembly and connector concealment.

The current evidence confirms the previous critic finding: chair_body is registered in the assembly manifest but rejected from display because its evaluated mesh remains degenerate. The reported candidate bounds and body-reference comparison do not establish visible compliance.
required_changes: chair_body: Locally replace or repair the degenerating chair_body construction—investigating the rounded_box hull operations, including the previously identified front_roll candidate—so no zero-area triangles remain. Confirm the full chair body displays in assembly.scene() while retaining its established bounds, symmetry, root transform, gray upholstery components, nailhead trim, and four underside slots. Keep the legs connected through the existing FixedAssembly.connect TabSlot interfaces and ensure their tabs are concealed by the restored body.
